original_question: Let f: P^n -> P^n be a critically finite rational map in the sense that there exist hypersurfaces V subset W subset P^n such that f maps P^n - W to P^n - V as a covering map. Are there nontrivial examples for which P^n - V is Kobayashi hyperbolic, and if so how do such maps behave dynamically?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered Problem under the heading "Critically finite rational maps on P^n" in C. McMullen's note "Geometrically finite maps and Kleinian groups," contained in arXiv:math/9201271.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual problem. It identifies the correct object (critically finite rational self-maps of projective space defined via a covering outside hypersurfaces), the correct extra hypothesis (that the complement P^n - V be Kobayashi hyperbolic), and the correct dynamical follow-up question. It also preserves the paper's narrow scope instead of broadening to general post-critically finite maps or unrelated hyperbolicity questions.
missing_details: The paper works on complex projective space P^n(C), and explicitly restricts to n > 1.
The defining hypersurfaces V ⊂ W ⊂ P^n are allowed to be possibly reducible.
The exact definition given in the surrounding text is: f : (P^n - W) -> (P^n - V) is a covering map.
The surrounding paragraph motivates V as the post-critical-set analogue: the intended setting is that the complement of the post-critical set be Kobayashi hyperbolic.
The paper phrases the problem as two direct questions, not conditionally: existence of nontrivial examples, and their dynamical behavior. Your phrase "and if so" slightly weakens that formulation.
No degree restriction or other extra algebraic hypothesis is imposed in the paper, so the refined question should not add any.
refined_question: For complex projective space P^n(C) with n > 1, are there nontrivial rational self-maps f : P^n -> P^n that are critically finite in the sense that there exist possibly reducible hypersurfaces V ⊂ W ⊂ P^n such that f : (P^n - W) -> (P^n - V) is a covering map, and for which P^n - V is Kobayashi hyperbolic? If so, how do such maps behave dynamically?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. In the paragraph immediately preceding the problem, McMullen explains that on the Riemann sphere the Poincare metric on the complement of the post-critical set is expanded by f, and suggests seeking the analogous higher-dimensional setting when the complement of the post-critical set is Kobayashi hyperbolic. He then gives the precise definition of a critically finite map via hypersurfaces V ⊂ W and the covering condition on complements, followed by the exact problem asking for nontrivial examples and their dynamics. Your draft is therefore essentially targeting this problem verbatim, but it should explicitly include n > 1, the complex projective setting, the allowance that V and W may be reducible, and the exact two-part wording of the problem.
